name: Asharelah
overview: Asharelah was a male Levite known as the son of Asaph, set apart to prophesy through musical instruments including lyres, harps, and cymbals. He was specifically chosen seventh by lot among the singers, highlighting his role in the sacred musical ministry of Israel. His service was part of the organized Levitical worship during the time recorded in 1 Chronicles.
namesAndTitles: The individual is primarily known as Asharelah, with an alternate form Jesharelah appearing in Scripture. Neither name is given a specific meaning in the biblical text, so they are simply proper names associated with this Levite musician.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Asharelah as the son of Asaph, linking him to a notable Levitical family known for temple music. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are detailed in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Asharelah's significance lies in his selection by lot to serve as a prophetic singer among the Levites, emphasizing the divine appointment of worship leaders in Israel. His musical role with lyres, harps, and cymbals demonstrates the integral part of music in proclaiming God's word and facilitating worship. Being chosen seventh among the singers indicates a structured and reverent approach to temple service, reflecting God's order in worship.
